Indicator_Name: Red List of Ecosystems
Units_Measure: RLE score (0–1 composite)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Ecosystem integrity; Spatial planning for biodiversity
Data_Source: JNCC / NatureScot RLE assessments
Climate_Rationale: IUCN RLE criteria include distributional change and functional disruption; climate is a key driver used in projecting future ecosystem collapse risk within RLE criteria C/D.
Framework_Classification: Component: IUCN Red List of Ecosystems score; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Ecosystem extent
Units_Measure: km² / % of land area
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Ecosystem integrity; Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Data_Source: JNCC; Countryside Survey; CEH land cover maps
Climate_Rationale: Extent figures are derived from land-cover mapping and habitat surveys; climate does not directly enter the calculation, though climate is a long-term driver of change.
Framework_Classification: Component: Extent of natural ecosystems; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Protected and conserved areas – total extent on land
Units_Measure: km² and % of land area
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; 30x30 -- protect land and sea
Data_Source: JNCC Protected Areas GIS / DEFRA
Climate_Rationale: Area of designated sites is a policy/legal measure; extent is recorded from designation registers, with no climate or weather data in the calculation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Total extent of protected areas on land; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Protected and conserved areas – total extent at sea
Units_Measure: km² and % of sea area
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; 30x30 -- protect land and sea
Data_Source: JNCC Marine Protected Areas register
Climate_Rationale: Marine protected area extent is a legal designation; area is calculated from GIS boundaries, not weather or climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Total extent of protected areas at sea; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Protected and conserved areas – SSSI condition
Units_Measure: % of SSSI area in favourable or recovering condition
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; 30x30 -- protect land and sea
Data_Source: Natural England / NatureScot / NRW SSSI condition data
Climate_Rationale: Condition assessments are based on field surveys of habitats and species. Favourable condition may be influenced by weather in individual assessment years, but weather data are not directly used in the scoring methodology.
Framework_Classification: Component: Condition of SSSIs in favourable or recovering condition; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Species Protection Index
Units_Measure: Index (0–100)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Ecosystem integrity; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: IUCN / JNCC species assessments
Climate_Rationale: SPI models protected-area coverage relative to species' range. Species distribution models underlying range estimates commonly use climate layers; climate is embedded in the modelling.
Framework_Classification: Component: Species Protection Index; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Birds of the wider countryside and at sea – all breeding birds
Units_Measure: Index (1970 = 100); geometric mean of species indices
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator C5; JNCC Wild Bird Populations
Data_Source: BTO / RSPB / JNCC Breeding Bird Survey (BBS); Common Bird Census (CBC)
Climate_Rationale: BBS counts are corrected for year-to-year variation. Bird population trends are strongly driven by climate; the TRIM model uses count data directly but inter-annual climate variability is a known confounder. Confidence intervals account for this variation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of all breeding birds; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Birds of the wider countryside and at sea – farmland birds
Units_Measure: Index (1970 = 100); 19 species
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: BTO / RSPB / JNCC BBS; CBC
Climate_Rationale: As above — population indices from BBS. Climate variability (e.g., cold springs, droughts) affects breeding productivity and hence counts, but weather data are not explicitly input to TRIM.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of breeding birds on farmland; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Birds of the wider countryside and at sea – woodland birds
Units_Measure: Index (1970 = 100); 37 species (25 specialists, 12 generalists)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: BTO / RSPB / JNCC BBS; CBC
Climate_Rationale: As above. Woodland bird trends are correlated with temperature and rainfall through effects on invertebrate food supply and breeding success; not directly modelled but a key source of inter-annual noise.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of breeding birds in woodland; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Birds of the wider countryside and at sea – wetland birds
Units_Measure: Index (1975 = 100); 26 species
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: BTO / RSPB / JNCC BBS; Waterways BBS (WBBS)
Climate_Rationale: Wetland bird abundance is particularly sensitive to rainfall, flooding and drought affecting habitat availability; BBS/WeBS counts reflect these effects though weather is not a direct model input.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of breeding wetland birds; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Birds of the wider countryside and at sea – seabirds
Units_Measure: Index (1986 = 100); ~25 species
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: JNCC Seabird Monitoring Programme (SMP)
Climate_Rationale: Seabird breeding success is strongly linked to sea surface temperature and prey availability (sandeel etc.), both driven by climate. SST data inform understanding of trends but are not directly input to the population index calculation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of breeding seabirds; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Birds of the wider countryside and at sea – upland birds
Units_Measure: Index (1994 = 100); upland specialist species
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: BTO / RSPB / JNCC BBS
Climate_Rationale: Upland bird populations are sensitive to weather (late snow, summer rainfall) affecting chick survival. BBS count data reflect these effects; weather not directly input.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of breeding upland birds; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Birds of the wider countryside and at sea – wintering waterbirds
Units_Measure: Index (1975/76 = 100); wildfowl and waders
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: BTO / JNCC / RSPB / WWT Wetland Bird Survey (WeBS); Goose & Swan Monitoring Programme
Climate_Rationale: WeBS counts of wintering waterbirds are strongly influenced by weather: hard winters cause movements and artificially inflate UK counts, mild winters do the opposite. Cold-weather movements are a formally recognised confounder and the data are analysed with this in mind.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of wintering waterbirds; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Insects of the wider countryside – all butterflies
Units_Measure: Index (1976 = 100); ~60 species
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: UK Butterfly Monitoring Scheme (UKBMS) – Butterfly Conservation / CEH / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: UKBMS transect counts are fundamentally a measure of flight activity, which is highly dependent on daily temperature and sunshine. The UKBMS methodology adjusts counts to a standard weather window, and site/year indices are generated with weather correction built in.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of all species of butterfly; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Insects of the wider countryside – habitat specialist butterflies
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: UKBMS – Butterfly Conservation / CEH / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: As above — habitat specialist counts use the same UKBMS methodology with weather-adjusted flight period counts.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of habitat specialist butterflies; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Insects of the wider countryside – generalist butterflies
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: UKBMS – Butterfly Conservation / CEH / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: As above.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of generalist butterflies; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Insects of the wider countryside – farmland specialist butterflies
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: UKBMS – Butterfly Conservation / CEH / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: As above.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of farmland specialist butterflies; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Insects of the wider countryside – woodland specialist butterflies
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: UKBMS – Butterfly Conservation / CEH / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: As above.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of woodland specialist butterflies; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Mammals of the wider countryside (bats)
Units_Measure: Index (1999 = 100); 12 bat species
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: Bat Conservation Trust / JNCC National Bat Monitoring Programme (NBMP)
Climate_Rationale: National Bat Monitoring Programme counts (walked and driven transects, static detector nights) are strongly influenced by temperature. Bats do not emerge below ~10°C; counts on cold nights are near zero. Survey protocols include weather thresholds, but weather still introduces significant year-to-year variation in effort-corrected indices.
Framework_Classification: Component: Change in the abundance of bat populations; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Plants of the wider countryside – arable field margins
Units_Measure: Index of plant species occurrence in habitat
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: Countryside Survey / BSBI recording
Climate_Rationale: National Plant Monitoring Scheme records plant presence/frequency in fixed plots. Plant community composition shifts with climate over decades but weather does not directly enter plot-visit data or trend calculations.
Framework_Classification: Component: Arable field margins; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Plants of the wider countryside – bog and wet heath
Units_Measure: Index of plant species occurrence in habitat
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: Countryside Survey / BSBI recording
Climate_Rationale: As above. Bog vegetation is sensitive to rainfall and drought over multi-year timescales, but individual survey visits do not use weather data in the calculation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Bog and wet heath; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Plants of the wider countryside – broadleaved woodland and hedges
Units_Measure: Index of plant species occurrence in habitat
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: Countryside Survey / BSBI recording
Climate_Rationale: As above.
Framework_Classification: Component: Broadleaved woodland and hedges; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Plants of the wider countryside – lowland grassland
Units_Measure: Index of plant species occurrence in habitat
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Data_Source: Countryside Survey / BSBI recording
Climate_Rationale: As above.
Framework_Classification: Component: Lowland grassland; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Status of priority species: relative abundance
Units_Measure: Index; multi-taxon priority species
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator C4a Priority species abundance
Data_Source: Various recording schemes collated by JNCC / Defra
Climate_Rationale: Multi-taxon abundance indicator aggregates recording scheme data across ~251 species using smoothing models. Several contributing schemes (butterflies, birds, bats) have weather-sensitive detection; climate is embedded in inter-annual variability of underlying count data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Relative abundance of priority species; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Status of priority species: distribution
Units_Measure: Index of number of occupied 10-km squares
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator C4b Priority species distribution
Data_Source: NBN Atlas / JNCC priority species data
Climate_Rationale: Occupancy modelling of 506 species using NBN Atlas records. Climate is a key driver of distribution change but is not an explicit input to the occupancy models; indirect effect through species range shifts.
Framework_Classification: Component: Distribution of UK priority species; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Conservation status of habitats of European importance (Habitats Regulations)
Units_Measure: % of habitats assessed as favourable or improving (Habitats Regulations)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator C3a Habitats Regulations habitats
Data_Source: JNCC / country nature conservation bodies Article 17 reporting
Climate_Rationale: Condition assessments based on 6-yearly Article 17 surveys and expert assessment. Weather conditions at the time of field surveys may affect observed condition but do not formally enter the assessment methodology.
Framework_Classification: Component: Percentage of habitats in favourable or improving conservation status; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Conservation status of species of European importance (Habitats Regulations)
Units_Measure: % of species assessed as favourable or improving (Habitats Regulations)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator C3b Habitats Regulations species
Data_Source: JNCC / country nature conservation bodies Article 17 reporting
Climate_Rationale: As above — 6-yearly population and range assessments; weather is a background driver but not a direct model input.
Framework_Classification: Component: Percentage of species in favourable or improving conservation status; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Sustainable fisheries – proportion of stocks harvested sustainably
Units_Measure: % of assessed stocks fished at or below FMSY
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Sustainable use of wild species
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator B2a Fish stocks sustainability
Data_Source: ICES stock assessments; Marine Management Organisation (MMO)
Climate_Rationale: ICES stock assessments use age/size-structured population models fitted to survey and commercial catch data. Sea temperature and oceanographic data inform stock productivity parameters and recruitment; climate is embedded in analytical stock models.
Framework_Classification: Component: Proportion of fish stocks harvested sustainably; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Sustainable fisheries – biomass of stocks at full reproductive capacity
Units_Measure: % of assessed stocks at or above Bpa (precautionary biomass reference point)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Sustainable use of wild species
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator B2b Fish stock biomass
Data_Source: ICES stock assessments; MMO
Climate_Rationale: As above — same ICES analytical frameworks. SST affects recruitment strength and stock productivity in the underlying models.
Framework_Classification: Component: Biomass of stocks at full reproductive capacity; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Fish size classes in the North Sea (mean maximum length)
Units_Measure: Mean maximum length (MML) of demersal fish community
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Sustainable use of wild species
Data_Source: ICES North Sea bottom trawl survey (IBTS)
Climate_Rationale: Mean maximum length is calculated from IBTS trawl survey catches. Sea temperature affects fish growth rates and species composition; climate data are not directly input but strongly influence community composition.
Framework_Classification: Component: Fish size in the North Sea; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Agricultural and forest ecosystem extent and condition – agri-environment schemes
Units_Measure: million hectares under scheme
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Data_Source: Defra / Natural England agri-environment statistics
Climate_Rationale: Area under agri-environment schemes is a policy/administrative measure derived from scheme application records. No climate or weather data used.
Framework_Classification: Component: Area of land in higher-level or targeted agri-environment schemes; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Agricultural and forest ecosystem extent and condition – sustainable forestry certification
Units_Measure: % and million hectares certified (UKWAS / FSC / PEFC)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Data_Source: Forestry Commission / Forest Research woodland statistics
Climate_Rationale: Area certified under UKWAS/FSC/PEFC is an administrative measure from certification registers; no climate data used.
Framework_Classification: Component: Area of forestry land certified as sustainably managed; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Habitat connectivity – butterflies and woodland birds (combined)
Units_Measure: Population synchrony index (0–100%)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Data_Source: UKBMS; BTO BBS — CEH / JNCC analysis
Climate_Rationale: Population synchrony index is calculated from BBS/UKBMS monitoring data. Weather events (e.g., cold springs) synchronise populations across sites, which can inflate or deflate synchrony estimates; climate variability is a known confounder.
Framework_Classification: Component: Habitat connectivity of butterflies and woodland birds; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Climate change – greenhouse gas emissions
Units_Measure: MtCO₂e/year (index, 1990 = 100)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Data_Source: DESNZ UK GHG Inventory
Climate_Rationale: UK GHG inventory uses activity data and emission factors; weather/climate enters only marginally (e.g., temperature affects heating demand). Buildings emissions are temperature-adjusted in the CCC's monitoring but not in the official GHG inventory itself.
Framework_Classification: Component: UK territorial GHG emissions; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pressure from climate change on biodiversity
Units_Measure: Index of species range exposure to climate change
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator B4 Climate change pressure
Data_Source: JNCC / CEH species distribution and climate modelling
Climate_Rationale: This is explicitly a climate indicator: it directly models the exposure of species' ranges to projected climate change using climate scenarios (e.g., UKCP18 projections). Temperature and rainfall projections are the primary inputs.
Framework_Classification: Component: Exposure of species to climate change (climate change vulnerability index); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pressure from air pollution – acidity critical loads exceedance
Units_Measure: % of ecosystem area in exceedance of critical load for acidity
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator B5a(i) Air pollution acidity
Data_Source: DEFRA / NAEI critical loads mapping; CEH
Climate_Rationale: Critical loads exceedance is calculated from atmospheric deposition modelling using emissions and meteorological data (wind, rainfall). Meteorological inputs affect deposition modelling, but the indicator tracks long-term trends rather than year-to-year weather variation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Area of land affected by acidity (critical loads exceedance); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pressure from air pollution – nitrogen critical loads exceedance
Units_Measure: % of ecosystem area in exceedance of critical load for nutrient N
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Reduce pollution to safe levels
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator B5a(ii) Air pollution nitrogen
Data_Source: DEFRA / NAEI critical loads mapping; CEH
Climate_Rationale: Nitrogen deposition modelling (CBED/FRAME) explicitly uses rainfall and atmospheric stability data to calculate wet and dry deposition. Meteorological data are a direct input to the deposition model, making this medium-high. Annual variability in rainfall and temperature affects the calculated deposition values.
Framework_Classification: Component: Area of land affected by nutrient nitrogen deposition (critical loads exceedance); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pressure from pollution – marine
Units_Measure: Index of hazardous substance inputs (combined index)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Reduce pollution to safe levels
Data_Source: EA / SEPA / Marine Management Organisation; OSPAR data
Climate_Rationale: Combined index of riverine, atmospheric and direct inputs of hazardous substances; flow data (which is climate-influenced) feeds into riverine loading estimates but climate/weather is not a primary driver of the trend.
Framework_Classification: Component: Combined input of hazardous substances into UK marine environment; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pressure from invasive non-native species – freshwater
Units_Measure: Cumulative number of established freshwater INNS
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Eliminate and control invasive alien species
Data_Source: GB Non-native Species Information Portal (NNSIP) / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: Cumulative establishment count from the NNSIP species list. Climate warming facilitates establishment of many INNS (temperature thresholds for reproduction), so climate is a background driver but not a direct model input.
Framework_Classification: Component: Established freshwater INNS – cumulative number; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pressure from invasive non-native species – marine
Units_Measure: Cumulative number of established marine INNS
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Eliminate and control invasive alien species
Data_Source: GB NNSIP / JNCC Marine Non-native Species register
Climate_Rationale: As above — sea surface temperature facilitates marine INNS establishment but climate data are not used in the calculation of cumulative counts.
Framework_Classification: Component: Established marine INNS – cumulative number; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pressure from invasive non-native species – terrestrial
Units_Measure: Cumulative number of established terrestrial INNS
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Eliminate and control invasive alien species
Data_Source: GB NNSIP / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: As above.
Framework_Classification: Component: Established terrestrial INNS – cumulative number; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pressure from invasive non-native species – establishment rate
Units_Measure: New INNS establishing per year
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Eliminate and control invasive alien species
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator B6d INNS establishment rate
Data_Source: GB NNSIP / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: Annual establishment rate from NNSIP; climate is a facilitating factor for establishment but not directly modelled.
Framework_Classification: Component: Rate of establishment of INNS; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Surface water status – WFD ecological status
Units_Measure: % of water bodies meeting good or high ecological status (WFD)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Reduce pollution to safe levels
Data_Source: Environment Agency / SEPA / NRW WFD assessments
Climate_Rationale: WFD ecological status classifications include biological quality elements (macrophytes, diatoms, invertebrates, fish) and physico-chemical elements. River flows and temperatures — both climate-driven — strongly affect these assessments. Low-flow years and high temperatures can push water bodies out of good status independently of pollution trends.
Framework_Classification: Component: Percentage of surface water bodies in good or high ecological status; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Greenhouse gas removals by forests
Units_Measure: MtCO₂e (cumulative net removals since baseline)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Restore and enhance nature's contributions to people
Data_Source: Forestry Commission / Forest Research; DESNZ UK GHG Inventory LULUCF
Climate_Rationale: Forest carbon flux is modelled using forest inventory data and carbon accounting models. Temperature and rainfall affect tree growth rates and hence carbon accumulation; the Forestry Commission carbon models (e.g., C-FLOW, Forest Yield) incorporate climate-adjusted growth parameters.
Framework_Classification: Component: Cumulative net removals of GHGs by UK forests; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Pollinating insects
Units_Measure: Index of occupancy (number of occupied 1-km squares) for wild bee & hoverfly species
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Restore and enhance nature's contributions to people
Data_Source: Pollinator Monitoring Scheme (PoMS) – CEH / JNCC / Defra
Climate_Rationale: PoMS transect and flower-insect timed counts are strongly weather-dependent (bees and hoverflies only fly in suitable conditions). Survey protocols include minimum weather thresholds, but detections still vary with temperature and sunshine on survey days.
Framework_Classification: Component: Occupancy of pollinating insects; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Genetic diversity of animal genetic resources – cattle breeds
Units_Measure: Number of breeds with population data / % at risk
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Genetic resources and benefit sharing
Data_Source: Rare Breeds Survival Trust; Defra / BCMS livestock data
Climate_Rationale: Census-based count of registered breeding animals from livestock databases; no climate data used.
Framework_Classification: Component: Number of UK cattle breeds monitored; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Genetic diversity of animal genetic resources – sheep breeds
Units_Measure: Number of breeds with population data / % at risk
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Genetic resources and benefit sharing
Data_Source: Rare Breeds Survival Trust; Defra livestock data
Climate_Rationale: As above.
Framework_Classification: Component: Number of UK sheep breeds monitored; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Genetic diversity – plant genetic resources
Units_Measure: Number of accessions in gene banks; % of target species held
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Genetic resources and benefit sharing
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator C9b Plant genetic resources
Data_Source: Kew Royal Botanic Gardens Millennium Seed Bank; SASA
Climate_Rationale: Count of accessions held in gene banks and seed collections; no climate data used in the calculation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Status of ex situ conservation of cultivated plants and their wild relatives; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Awareness, understanding and support for conservation (public awareness)
Units_Measure: % of people with positive responses (survey)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Means of implementation; Knowledge and data for decision-making
Data_Source: DEFRA Public Attitudes Tracker / survey
Climate_Rationale: Survey-based measure of public attitudes; no climate or weather data used.
Framework_Classification: Component: Public awareness and understanding of biodiversity; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Taking action for nature – conservation volunteering (volunteer time)
Units_Measure: Hours per year / number of volunteers
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Means of implementation; Participation and rights of indigenous peoples
Data_Source: NCVO / FWAG / Wildlife Trusts / RSPB volunteering data
Climate_Rationale: Count of volunteer hours from organisational returns; no climate data used. (Weather may marginally affect volunteer turnout on survey days, but is not formally accounted for.)
Framework_Classification: Component: Volunteer time spent in nature conservation; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Integration of biodiversity into decision-making (survey-based)
Units_Measure: Index / survey of integration into policy and planning
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Means of implementation; Mainstream biodiversity across all sectors
Data_Source: Survey of policy-makers / DEFRA assessment
Climate_Rationale: Policy/survey indicator; no climate data used.
Framework_Classification: Component: Biodiversity integrated into local and national decision-making; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Value of biodiversity – natural capital accounts
Units_Measure: £ billion (total ecosystem services value, ONS Natural Capital Accounts)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Means of implementation; Mobilise USD 200bn/year for biodiversity
Data_Source: ONS UK Natural Capital Accounts
Climate_Rationale: ONS Natural Capital Accounts value ecosystem service flows. Some services (water supply, recreation) are influenced by weather in individual account years, but valuation methodology does not formally adjust for weather.
Framework_Classification: Component: Value of ecosystem services in UK natural capital accounts; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Global biodiversity impacts of UK consumption – deforestation footprint
Units_Measure: km² of deforestation attributable to UK imports of key commodities
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Business assessment and disclosure of biodiversity; Enable sustainable consumption choices
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Global consumption impacts indicator (formerly A4/GEIC)
Data_Source: Global Environmental Impacts of Consumption model – JNCC / SEI / DEFRA
Climate_Rationale: Deforestation footprint of UK consumption modelled through trade data and land-use change statistics; climate does not directly enter the IOTA/GLORIA calculation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Area of deforestation worldwide associated with UK consumption; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Expenditure on biodiversity – UK public sector
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Finance | Governance, Society & Data
Units_Measure: £ million/year (government spending on biodiversity)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Mobilise USD 200bn/year for biodiversity
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator E2a Public biodiversity spending
Data_Source: HM Treasury PESA; DEFRA spending review data
Climate_Rationale: Administrative financial data from government accounts; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Public sector expenditure on biodiversity in the UK; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Expenditure on biodiversity – NGO and private sector
Units_Measure: £ million/year
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Mobilise USD 200bn/year for biodiversity
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator E2b NGO / private biodiversity spending
Data_Source: NCVO / Wildlife Trusts / RSPB financial returns
Climate_Rationale: Organisational financial returns; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Non-governmental and private sector spending on biodiversity; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Expenditure on biodiversity – international ODA
Units_Measure: £ million/year (UK ODA for biodiversity)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Mobilise USD 200bn/year for biodiversity
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator E2c International biodiversity ODA
Data_Source: FCDO ODA statistics; OECD biodiversity-relevant aid marker
Climate_Rationale: ODA spending data with Rio Markers; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: International development spending on biodiversity; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Biodiversity data for decision making
Units_Measure: Number of records downloaded; download events; number of users (NBN Atlas)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Knowledge and data for decision-making
Data_Source: National Biodiversity Network (NBN) Atlas
Climate_Rationale: Usage statistics (downloads, users) from the NBN Atlas system; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Use of biodiversity records in the NBN Atlas; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Protected and conserved areas – Part A: land meeting 30x30 criteria
Units_Measure: % of UK land meeting 30x30 criteria (in development)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; 30x30 -- protect land and sea
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator A3 Part A (new 2025); jncc.gov.uk/our-work/ukbi-protected-areas
Data_Source: JNCC / country nature conservation bodies; national 30x30 assessment frameworks
Climate_Rationale: Area-based assessment of land meeting 30x30 criteria; derived from GIS and management data, no climate input.
Framework_Classification: Component: Part A: Land protected or conserved and effectively managed for biodiversity (30x30); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Protected and conserved areas – Part C: OECMs
Units_Measure: Area (ha) of OECMs; % contributing to 30x30
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; 30x30 -- protect land and sea
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator A3 Part C; jncc.gov.uk/our-work/ukbi-protected-areas
Data_Source: NatureScot OECM assessment (Scotland only; other countries in development)
Climate_Rationale: Administrative designation area data; no climate input.
Framework_Classification: Component: Part C: OECMs — land outside formally protected areas managed for biodiversity; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Protected and conserved areas – Part D: A/SSSI feature condition
Units_Measure: % of A/SSSI features in favourable or unfavourable-recovering condition
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; 30x30 -- protect land and sea
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Indicator A3 Part D; jncc.gov.uk/our-work/ukbi-protected-areas
Data_Source: Natural England; NatureScot; NRW; NIEA A/SSSI condition data
Climate_Rationale: Feature condition scores from field surveys. Weather in the survey year may affect observed plant and invertebrate condition scores, but climate data are not formally used in the condition methodology.
Framework_Classification: Component: Part D: Condition of A/SSSI features (favourable or unfavourable-recovering); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Red List Index
Units_Measure: Index (0–1); 0 = all extinct, 1 = all Least Concern; weighted by UK range
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Ecosystem integrity; Halt extinction, recover species; UN SDG 15.5 (Halt biodiversity loss)
Data_Source: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species; global range data weighted by UK proportion
Climate_Rationale: Global RLI is based on IUCN Red List assessments which explicitly consider climate change as a threat under threat category 11. Reassessments of species' range and population trend incorporate climate-driven range shifts, so climate data inform assessments indirectly.
Framework_Classification: Component: Red List Index of UK species (global extinction risk weighted by UK range proportion); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Genetic diversity of wild species
Units_Measure: % of species populations with Ne ≥ 500
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Ecosystem integrity; Halt extinction, recover species
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Genetic diversity of wild species (new 2025 GBF headline); jncc.gov.uk/our-work/ukbi-genetic-diversity-of-wild-species
Data_Source: SEFARI / Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh / NatureScot / Univ. Edinburgh / RBG Kew — expert elicitation and genetic scorecard data
Climate_Rationale: Effective population size estimates from genetic scorecard data and expert elicitation. Climate is a background stressor affecting population viability but does not directly enter the Ne calculation methodology.
Framework_Classification: Component: Proportion of populations with effective population size ≥500 (Ne ≥ 500); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Spring Index (phenology)
Units_Measure: Mean day-of-year of 4 spring events (days after 31 December)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Minimise climate change impacts on biodiversity
Data_Source: UK Phenology Network (Nature's Calendar / Woodland Trust); Royal Meteorological Society (historic)
Climate_Rationale: This is an explicitly climate-driven indicator. The Spring Index is the mean day-of-year of 4 phenological events directly correlated with spring temperature (Central England Temperature). Temperature is the primary explanatory variable and the indicator is explicitly analysed against CET.
Framework_Classification: Component: Timing of biological spring events (hawthorn, horse chestnut flowering; orange-tip butterfly; swallow arrival); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Services provided by ecosystems
Units_Measure: Physical flow (various units) and monetary value (£ million/year) of provisioning, regulating and cultural services
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Sustaining nature's contributions to people; Restore and enhance nature's contributions to people
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Services provided by ecosystems (new GBF headline B.1); jncc.gov.uk/our-work/ukbi-services-provided-by-ecosystems
Data_Source: ONS UK Natural Capital Accounts (with Defra support)
Climate_Rationale: ONS NCA ecosystem service flows include weather-sensitive services (e.g., water provision, carbon sequestration in a given year), but valuation methodology uses average flow data; weather is not formally adjusted for in the calculation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Physical and monetary flow of ecosystem services relevant to biodiversity; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Green and blue space in built-up areas
Units_Measure: % of urban area that is accessible green or blue space
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Green and blue spaces in urban areas; UN SDG 11.7 (Safe green and public spaces)
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Green and blue space in built-up areas (new GBF headline); jncc.gov.uk/our-work/ukbi-green-and-blue-space-in-built-up-areas
Data_Source: ONS Urban Natural Capital Accounts; Ordnance Survey Greenspace Layer
Climate_Rationale: Based on GIS mapping of green/blue space from OS Greenspace Layer and ONS urban habitat accounts; static spatial data with no weather or climate inputs.
Framework_Classification: Component: Proportion of accessible green and blue space within urban areas; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Biodiversity and business
Units_Measure: % of large businesses with certified EMS (ISO 14001 or EMAS)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Business assessment and disclosure of biodiversity
Data_Source: BSI / UKAS accreditation register; ISO 14001 certification data
Climate_Rationale: Count of ISO 14001/EMAS certifications from accreditation registers; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Proportion of large UK businesses with an environmental management system (EMS); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Biodiversity disclosures
Units_Measure: Number of UK-registered large companies disclosing biodiversity risks and impacts
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Business assessment and disclosure of biodiversity
Data_Source: TNFD adopter register; CDP biodiversity responses; World Benchmarking Alliance (WBA)
Climate_Rationale: Count of company disclosures from TNFD register, CDP responses, WBA assessments; no climate data in the counting methodology.
Framework_Classification: Component: Number of large UK companies making biodiversity-related disclosures (TNFD, CDP, WBA); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Global biodiversity impacts of UK consumption – species loss risk (GLORIA)
Units_Measure: LIFE score (expected species extinctions); species richness-weighted ha; predicted regional species loss
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Business assessment and disclosure of biodiversity; Enable sustainable consumption choices
Source_Reference: UKBI 2025 – Global biodiversity impacts (revised GLORIA methodology); jncc.gov.uk/our-work/ukbi-global-biodiversity-impact
Data_Source: IOTA framework (Croft et al.) using GLORIA input-output model; FAO; Chaudhary & Kastner (2016) characterisation factors
Climate_Rationale: IOTA/GLORIA consumption-based deforestation and species-loss model uses trade and land-use data; climate is not a direct input to the modelling framework, though deforestation rates are indirectly influenced by climate variability.
Framework_Classification: Component: Deforestation and species loss risk linked to UK consumption of key commodities; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Awareness, understanding and support for conservation (public concern)
Units_Measure: % of adults expressing concern or awareness (Defra public attitudes tracker)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Knowledge and data for decision-making
Data_Source: Defra Public Attitudes and Behaviours Tracker (PABT)
Climate_Rationale: Survey-based; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Public awareness and concern about biodiversity loss; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Integration of biodiversity into decision-making (under review – no current data)
Units_Measure: No current measurable indicator — development paused
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Means of implementation; Mainstream biodiversity across all sectors
Data_Source: No active data source — indicator under review for GBF alignment
Climate_Rationale: No active indicator; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Biodiversity integrated into national and local planning and decision-making; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Expenditure on biodiversity – UK international ODA
Units_Measure: £ million/year (UK international biodiversity ODA + multilateral contributions)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Means of implementation; Mobilise USD 200bn/year for biodiversity
Data_Source: FCDO ODA statistics (Rio Markers); OECD DAC; GEF / GCF / GBFF contribution data
Climate_Rationale: Financial data from ODA and multilateral fund records; no climate data in calculation. Note: some funding streams (e.g., GCF) overlap with climate finance but the indicator measures expenditure amounts, not climate outcomes.
Framework_Classification: Component: UK public sector spending on international biodiversity (ODA, OTEP, GEF, GCF, GBFF); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Fish size classes in the North Sea – mean maximum length
Units_Measure: Mean maximum length (cm) of fish caught in standard trawl surveys
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Sustainable use of wild species
Data_Source: ICES North Sea International Bottom Trawl Survey (NS-IBTS)
Climate_Rationale: IBTS trawl survey catches. Sea temperature directly affects fish growth rates, species assemblage and gear catchability; climate is embedded in inter-annual variability though not directly input to MML calculation.
Framework_Classification: Component: Mean maximum length (MML) of demersal fish community in North Sea; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Surface water status – WFD ecological status (revised)
Units_Measure: % of classified water bodies in good or high ecological status
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Reduce pollution to safe levels
Data_Source: Environment Agency; SEPA; Natural Resources Wales — WFD classification assessments
Climate_Rationale: As per row 44 — WFD status assessments are influenced by temperature and flow (both climate-driven); biological elements particularly sensitive to low-flow warm years.
Framework_Classification: Component: Percentage of surface water bodies in good or high ecological status (WFD); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Habitat connectivity – butterflies (population synchrony)
Units_Measure: Population synchrony index (correlation of population growth rates across sites)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Data_Source: UK Butterfly Monitoring Scheme (UKBMS) — CEH / Butterfly Conservation / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: Population synchrony for butterflies calculated from UKBMS transect data. Shared weather events (warm or cold spring) synchronise flight periods across sites; weather is a major driver of synchrony and is the primary confounder the indicator aims to account for by differentiating weather-driven from structural connectivity.
Framework_Classification: Component: Population synchrony index for butterflies across monitoring sites; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Habitat connectivity – woodland birds (population synchrony)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Governance, Society & Data
Units_Measure: Population synchrony index (correlation of population growth rates across BBS sites)
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Restore 30% of degraded ecosystems
Data_Source: BTO Breeding Bird Survey (BBS) — BTO / RSPB / JNCC
Climate_Rationale: Population synchrony for woodland birds from BBS data. Cold springs and weather events synchronise breeding productivity across sites; weather is an important confounder for synchrony measures.
Framework_Classification: Component: Population synchrony index for woodland birds across monitoring sites; Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Taking action for nature – conservation volunteering
Units_Measure: Million hours/year of formal nature conservation volunteering
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Means of implementation; Participation and rights of indigenous peoples
Data_Source: Wildlife Trusts; RSPB; National Trust; BTCV — annual volunteer data returns
Climate_Rationale: Organisational volunteer hour returns; no climate data in calculation. Bad weather marginally reduces volunteer activity but this is not formally accounted for.
Framework_Classification: Component: Hours per year spent in formal conservation volunteering (Wildlife Trusts, RSPB, etc.); Assessed: 2025

Indicator_Name: Agricultural and forest ecosystem extent and condition – woodland certification
Units_Measure: % of woodland area with UKWAS / FSC / PEFC certification
Policy_Goal: UK Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; Environment Act 2021 species targets; Sustainable use of wild species; Sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, forestry and fisheries
Data_Source: Forestry Commission / Forest Research UK woodland statistics
Climate_Rationale: Administrative certification area data; no climate data.
Framework_Classification: Component: Area of woodland in UK assessed as sustainably managed (certified); Assessed: 2025
